Ele {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou para libertar os que são esmagados pelos outros \v 19 e para dizer: 'Este é o ano em que o Senhor vai mostrar bondade ao {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 61:1-2, with a line from Isaiah 58:6, from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek of Isaiah 61:1-2. The line "to send away the oppressed in release" comes from Isaiah 58:6, where God describes the fast he wants. The reading stops before "the day of vengeance of our God". In Isaiah the speaker is the one anointed to bring good news to Zion; Jesus says it is fulfilled in him (4:21). "Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: anointed: set apart by God for a task, as kings, priests and prophets were anointed with oil
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the title Christ, "the anointed one". Jesus was anointed with the Spirit at his baptism (3:22; Acts 10:38).

decisions.choice: release: freedom, the same word as "forgiveness" in 1:77 and 3:3
decisions.reason: The word means a setting free, from debts, prison or sins. Luke uses it both for forgiveness and here for release; the two are not separated.

decisions.choice: the year of the Lord's favor: the year of release in the Law, the Jubilee
decisions.reason: In the Jubilee, every fiftieth year, release was proclaimed through the land; debts were canceled and land returned to its families (Leviticus 25:10). Isaiah uses the picture for God's coming salvation.

decisions.choice: recovery of sight to the blind: as in the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: the opening of prison to the bound, as the Hebrew of Isaiah 61:1 can be read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew line can mean release from darkness for prisoners; the Greek version, which Luke quotes, has sight for the blind. Jesus will give sight to the blind (7:21-22; 18:35-43).

decisions.choice: no "to heal the brokenhearted" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: adds "to heal the brokenhearted" after "he has sent me"
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts do not have the line; many later ones add it from Isaiah 61:1. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: me (with the capital-pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Jesus reads the words as spoken about himself (4:21), so "me" is a pronoun for Jesus, and "he" is a pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says what the anointing means; Literal and Balanced keep the word, which links to "Christ".

decisions.choice: 'This is the year when the Lord will show kindness to his people.'
alternatives: to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor
decisions.reason: Readable puts the announcement into words that can be said aloud. "His people" is supplied from the context of Isaiah 61.

decisions.choice: the downtrodden
decisions.reason: The word means people who are broken or crushed.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Jesus reads these words of himself, so the pronouns for him take the span as in the English; a sentence that begins with "Me" is capitalised either way and has none.

decisions.choice: anunciar buenas noticias (L, B); contar la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is rendered as what it says, announcing good news; "evangelizar" now suggests a church activity, and "evangelio" is kept for the noun that names the message.

decisions.choice: m’a oint (L); m’a consacré par l’onction (B); m’a choisi (R)
decisions.reason: Anointing sets someone apart for a task (m2). Literal keeps the verb "oindre", which links to "Christ"; its forms are rare in speech, so Balanced says "consacré par l’onction", which keeps the image, and Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: le Seigneur montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur (B)
alternatives: l’année de la faveur du Seigneur
decisions.reason: French "montrer" needs an object, so Balanced supplies the possessive, which is a pronoun for God and carries the setting where the English has none.

decisions.choice: kuwaletea habari njema
decisions.reason: The verb is rendered as what it says, bringing good news, at every level; "Injili" is kept for the noun that names the message.

decisions.choice: amenipaka mafuta
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of anointing with oil (meaning decision m2); Readable says "amenichagua", as the English Readable says "chosen".

decisions.choice: the speaker of Isaiah's words says "{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}"; the Lord who anoints him is "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}"
decisions.reason: Jesus reads the words aloud and in 4:21 says they are fulfilled in him, so the English gives "me" the capital-pronoun setting; Vietnamese gives the speaker the word Jesus uses for himself. "tôi" would make him sound like any reader of the scroll.

decisions.choice: "tự do" for both occurrences of the word for release
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes one Greek word, the same as "forgiveness" in 1:77 and 3:3; Literal keeps one Vietnamese word for both lines, and Balanced and Readable keep the word "tự do" in the first line.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for kyrios in Isaiah's words, with no divine-name setting
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, so Vietnamese writes "Chúa" as the English writes "Lord" (style guide 7a); the Hebrew of Isaiah 61 has the divine name.

decisions.choice: "주님" for kyrios in the Isaiah quotation, with no divine_name span; the Spirit takes the honorific ("[계시다]", "임하셨다", "계신다")
decisions.reason: Isaiah 61:1 has the divine name in Hebrew, but Luke quotes the Greek, which has kyrios; Korean writes "주님", as for other New Testament quotations. Literal brackets the verb the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: "놓임" ... "놓아" (L, B) for aphesis, used twice
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the same word means release and forgiveness; Literal and Balanced keep one Korean root for both occurrences so the repetition shows.

decisions.choice: libertação ... em liberdade (L); liberdade ... em liberdade (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one word twice, for release and, elsewhere, forgiveness (m3). Here it is release, so Portuguese repeats the family of "liberdade" both times, as far as the sentence allows, and keeps "perdão" for the places where the word means forgiveness.

decisions.choice: os oprimidos
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "downtrodden" because the word means crushed. Portuguese "oprimido" still carries the picture of being pressed down and is the natural word for people crushed by others, so Balanced keeps it; Readable says "esmagados pelos outros", as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having rolled up the scroll having given back to the attendant he sat down; and of all the eyes in the synagogue were fixed on him.

en.L: And having rolled up the scroll and given [it] back to the attendant, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He rolled the scroll up again, handed it back to the attendant, and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat. All the eyes in the synagogue were fixed on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus closed the scroll and handed it back to the man in charge. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down. Everyone in the synagogue was staring at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y habiendo enrollado el rollo y devuelto [este] al asistente, se sentó; y los ojos de todos los [que estaban] en la sinagoga se clavaban en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Enrolló de nuevo el rollo, se lo devolvió al asistente y se sentó. Todas las miradas en la sinagoga estaban puestas en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús cerró el rollo y se lo devolvió al encargado. Luego se sentó. Todos en la sinagoga {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} miraban fijamente.

fr.L: Et, ayant replié le rouleau [et l’]ayant rendu au servant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’assit ; et les yeux de tous dans la synagogue étaient fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Il referma le rouleau, le rendit au servant de la synagogue et s’assit. Dans la synagogue, tous avaient les yeux fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus a refermé le rouleau et il l’a rendu à l’homme qui s’occupait de la synagogue. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est assis. Tous les gens dans la synagogue avaient les yeux fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Na akiisha kulikunja gombo na kumrudishia mhudumu, aliketi; na macho ya wote katika sinagogi yalikuwa yakimkazia.
sw.B: Alilikunja gombo tena, akamrudishia mhudumu, akaketi. Watu wote ndani ya sinagogi walikuwa wakimtazama kwa makini.
sw.R: Yesu alilifunga gombo na kumrudishia mhudumu wa sinagogi. Kisha akaketi. Kila mtu katika sinagogi alikuwa akimtazama sana.

ko.L: 그리고 두루마리를 말아 시중드는 사람에게 돌려주시고 앉으셨다. 그러자 회당에 있는 모든 사람의 눈이 그분께 쏠려 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 두루마리를 다시 말아 회당 일을 맡은 사람에게 돌려주시고 자리에 앉으셨다. 회당 안의 모든 사람이 예수를 뚫어지게 바라보았다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 두루마리를 말아서 회당을 돌보는 사람에게 돌려주셨다. 그리고 자리에 앉으셨다. 회당에 있던 사람들이 모두 예수를 뚫어지게 쳐다보았다.

vi.L: Và cuộn sách lại, trả cho người phục vụ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngồi xuống; và mắt của mọi người trong nhà hội đều chăm chú nhìn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài cuộn sách lại, trả cho người phục vụ, rồi ngồi xuống. Mọi con mắt trong nhà hội đều chăm chú nhìn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu cuộn sách lại và trả cho người coi sóc nhà hội. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngồi xuống. Mọi người trong nhà hội đều nhìn chăm chăm vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: E, tendo fechado o rolo e [o] devolvido ao assistente, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se sentou; e os olhos de todos na sinagoga estavam fixos {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.B: Ele fechou o rolo, o devolveu ao assistente e se sentou. Todos os olhos na sinagoga estavam fixos {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.R: Jesus fechou o rolo e o devolveu ao homem encarregado. Depois se sentou. Todos na sinagoga estavam olhando fixamente para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

decisions.choice: the attendant: the synagogue official who looked after the scrolls
decisions.reason: The word is used for an assistant or officer. In the synagogue he kept the sacred scrolls and handed them to the reader.

decisions.choice: he sat down: the position of a teacher about to explain the reading
alternatives: he had finished and sat down to listen
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach (5:3; Matthew 5:1). The people wait for him to speak.

source.text: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: He began then to say to them that Today has been fulfilled the scripture this in the ears of you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say to them, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears."
en.B: He began by telling them, "Today, as you have been listening, these words of Scripture have come true."
en.R: He said to them, "What you just heard {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} read has come true today!"

es.L: Y empezó a decirles: «Hoy se ha cumplido esta Escritura en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} oídos».
es.B: Comenzó diciéndoles: «Hoy, mientras {{plural_you:ustedes escuchaban|vosotros escuchabais}}, estas palabras de la Escritura se han cumplido».
es.R: Entonces les dijo: «¡Hoy se ha cumplido lo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:acaban|acabáis}} de oír leer!».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à leur dire : « Aujourd’hui cette Écriture a été accomplie à vos oreilles. »
fr.B: Il se mit à leur dire : « Aujourd’hui, pendant que vous écoutiez, ces paroles de l’Écriture se sont réalisées. »
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez entendu lire s’est réalisé aujourd’hui ! »

sw.L: Naye akaanza kuwaambia kwamba, "Leo andiko hili limetimizwa katika masikio yenu."
sw.B: Alianza kwa kuwaambia, "Leo, mlipokuwa mkisikiliza, maneno haya ya Maandiko yametimia."
sw.R: Aliwaambia, "Yale mliyonisikia nikisoma yametimia leo!"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하기 시작하셨다. "오늘 이 성경 말씀이 너희 귀에 이루어졌다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하기 시작하셨다. "너희가 듣는 가운데, 오늘 이 성경 말씀이 이루어졌다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 방금 읽은 말씀을 너희가 들었다. 그 말씀이 오늘 이루어졌다!"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu nói với họ: "Hôm nay lời Kinh Thánh này đã được ứng nghiệm trong tai các người."
vi.B: Ngài bắt đầu nói với họ: "Hôm nay, ngay khi các người đang nghe, lời Kinh Thánh này đã được ứng nghiệm."
vi.R: Ngài nói với họ: "Những lời các người vừa nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đọc, hôm nay đã thành sự thật!"

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} começou a lhes dizer: "Hoje esta Escritura se cumpriu nos ouvidos de vocês."
pt.B: Ele começou dizendo a eles: "Hoje, enquanto vocês ouviam, estas palavras da Escritura se cumpriram."
pt.R: Ele disse a eles: "Hoje aconteceu o que vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouviram ler!"

decisions.choice: today ... fulfilled: what Isaiah announced is happening now, in Jesus
alternatives: it will be fulfilled one day
decisions.reason: The perfect tense "has been fulfilled" means the fulfillment has taken place and stands. "Today" is a key word in Luke (2:11; 19:9; 23:43).

decisions.choice: in your ears: as you heard it
alternatives: the Scripture is fulfilled by your hearing it
decisions.reason: The phrase means "in your hearing": the reading they have just heard is coming true before them.

decisions.choice: as you have been listening (B); What you just heard me read (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. "Me" in Readable is Jesus speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}}, {{plural_you:ustedes escuchaban|vosotros escuchabais}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you", pronoun or verb, is the plural_you setting: the ustedes form by default, the vosotros form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the synagogue as "các người" (4:21-27)
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to a crowd, as in Mark 6 when he speaks in the same town; the warmer words for fellow townspeople would read as a sermon formula.

source.text: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: And all were bearing witness to him and were marveling at the words of the grace coming out of the mouth of him, and they were saying, Not son is of Joseph this?

en.L: And all were bearing witness to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and marveling at the words of grace coming out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, and they were saying, "Is this not [the] son of Joseph?"
en.B: Everyone there was speaking in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} favor, and they wondered at the words of grace that came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. And they kept saying, "Is this not Joseph's son?"
en.R: Everyone said good things about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were amazed that such kind and beautiful words came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. They said, "Is this not Joseph's son?"

es.L: Y todos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daban testimonio, y se asombraban ante las palabras de la gracia que brotaban de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca, y decían: «¿Acaso no es este [el] hijo de José?».
es.B: Todos hablaban a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} favor y se admiraban de las palabras llenas de gracia que salían de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca. Y decían una y otra vez: «¿No es este el hijo de José?».
es.R: Todos decían cosas buenas de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Estaban asombrados de que de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca salieran palabras tan amables y hermosas. Decían: «¿No es este el hijo de José?».

fr.L: Et tous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendaient témoignage et s’étonnaient des paroles de grâce qui sortaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche, et ils disaient : « Celui-ci n’est-il pas [le] fils de Joseph ? »
fr.B: Tous parlaient en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur et s’émerveillaient des paroles pleines de grâce qui sortaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche. Et ils répétaient : « N’est-ce pas le fils de Joseph ? »
fr.R: Tout le monde disait du bien de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Les gens s’étonnaient d’entendre sortir de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche des paroles si belles et si pleines de bonté. Ils disaient : « Ce n’est pas le fils de Joseph, celui-là ? »

sw.L: Na wote walikuwa wakitoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na kushangaa kwa ajili ya maneno ya neema yaliyotoka katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, nao walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"
sw.B: Kila mtu pale alimsema vizuri, na walishangazwa na maneno ya neema yaliyotoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Wakawa wakisema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"
sw.R: Wote walisema mambo mazuri juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Walishangaa kwamba maneno mazuri na ya upole kiasi hicho yalitoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Wakasema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"

ko.L: 그리고 모두가 그분을 좋게 증언하며, 그분의 입에서 나오는 은혜의 말씀에 놀라워하고 있었다. 그리고 그들이 말하고 있었다. "이 사람은 요셉의 아들이 아니냐?"
ko.B: 모든 사람이 예수를 좋게 말하였고, 그분의 입에서 나오는 은혜로운 말씀에 놀랐다. 그리고 그들은 "이 사람은 요셉의 아들이 아니냐?" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 사람들은 모두 예수를 칭찬하였다. 예수의 입에서 그렇게 은혜롭고 아름다운 말씀이 나오는 것을 보고 놀랐다. 그들은 "이 사람은 요셉의 아들이 아니냐?" 하고 말했다.

vi.L: Và mọi người đều làm chứng tốt cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và ngạc nhiên về những lời ân điển ra từ miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ nói: "Người này chẳng phải là con của Giô-sép sao?"
vi.B: Mọi người ở đó đều khen ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và lấy làm lạ về những lời đầy ân điển từ miệng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói ra. Họ cứ nói: "Ông ấy chẳng phải là con của Giô-sép sao?"
vi.R: Ai cũng nói tốt về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ rất ngạc nhiên vì những lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói thật tốt đẹp và đầy ân điển. Họ nói: "Ông ấy chẳng phải là con của Giô-sép sao?"

pt.L: E todos davam testemunho a favor {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e se admiravam das palavras de graça que saíam da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca, e diziam: "Este não é [o] filho de José?"
pt.B: Todos ali falavam a favor {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e se maravilhavam com as palavras de graça que saíam da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca. E diziam: "Este não é o filho de José?"
pt.R: Todos falavam bem {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Ficavam admirados com as palavras bonitas e cheias de bondade que saíam da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca. Eles diziam: "Este não é o filho de José?"

decisions.choice: words of grace: gracious words, full of charm and kindness, and speaking of God's favor
decisions.reason: The noun is the usual word for grace. With "words" it describes speech that is pleasing and kind (Colossians 4:6). The words were also about God's favor to the poor and captive (4:18-19). Literal and Balanced keep "grace"; Readable gives the sense the hearers felt.

decisions.choice: were bearing witness to him: they spoke well of him
decisions.reason: With this construction the verb means to speak in favor of someone. The mood changes only after Jesus' reply (4:28).

decisions.choice: Is this not the son of Joseph?: they expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is surprise that a local man, whose family they know, speaks like this. Luke has said that Jesus was thought to be Joseph's son (3:23).

decisions.choice: such kind and beautiful words
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the phrase, as the meaning decision on the word explains.

decisions.choice: "Người này" (L); "Ông ấy" (B, R) in the townspeople's question, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The townspeople still speak well of him here (meaning decisions), so Balanced and Readable use the respectful "ông ấy", as the crowd does in Mark 1:27, not the colder "ông ta"; Literal keeps the Greek's "this one".

decisions.choice: "ân điển" kept at Readable
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "kind and beautiful words"; Vietnamese keeps the key term "ân điển" beside "tốt đẹp", since the meaning decision says the words both charmed and spoke of God's favor.

decisions.choice: "은혜" kept at every level ("은혜의 말씀", "은혜로운 말씀", "은혜롭고 아름다운 말씀")
decisions.reason: Grace is a key term; the meaning decision reads both charm and God's favor in the phrase, and "은혜롭다" carries both in Korean.

decisions.choice: The townspeople speak of Jesus as "이 사람", with no honorific
decisions.reason: They know him as Joseph's son, as in Mark 6:2-3 in Korean; the narrator keeps the honorific.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Surely you will say to me the proverb this, Physician, heal yourself; what we heard having happened in the Capernaum do also here in the hometown of you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Surely you will say to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} this proverb: 'Physician, heal {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}! What we heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hometown.'"
en.B: He said to them, "No doubt you will quote this saying to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: 'Doctor, cure {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}!' And you will tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Do here in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own town the things we heard {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did in Capernaum.'"
en.R: Jesus said to them, "I am sure you will tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the old saying, 'Doctor, first make {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} well!' You will say, 'We heard about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did in Capernaum. Do the same things here in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hometown!'"

es.L: Y les dijo: «Seguramente {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:citarán|citaréis}} este proverbio: “Médico, sánate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo; todo lo que oímos que pasó en Cafarnaúm, hazlo también aquí en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} patria”».
es.B: Les dijo: «Sin duda {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:van|vais}} a citar este dicho: “¡Doctor, cúrate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo!”. Y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “Haz aquí, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propia tierra, lo que oímos que hiciste en Cafarnaúm”».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Estoy seguro de que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}} el viejo dicho: “Doctor, ¡primero sánate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo!”. También {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “Oímos lo que hiciste en Cafarnaúm. ¡Haz lo mismo aquí, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propio pueblo!”».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Assurément vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} direz ce proverbe : “Médecin, guéris-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême ! Tout ce que nous avons appris qui s’est passé à Capharnaüm, fais[-le] aussi ici, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} patrie.” »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Sans doute allez-vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} citer ce dicton : “Médecin, guéris-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême !” Et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} direz : “Ce que nous avons appris que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait à Capharnaüm, fais-le donc ici aussi, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} propre ville.” »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Je suis sûr que vous allez {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dire le vieux proverbe : “Médecin, commence par {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} soigner {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême !” Vous allez dire : “Nous avons entendu parler de ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait à Capharnaüm. Fais la même chose ici, dans la ville où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as grandi !” »

sw.L: Na akawaambia, "Kwa hakika mtaniambia methali hii: 'Mganga, jitibu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}! Mambo yote tuliyosikia yamefanyika Kapernaumu, yafanye pia hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani.'"
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Bila shaka mtanitajia msemo huu: 'Daktari, jitibu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!' Tena mtaniambia, 'Yafanye hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani yale tuliyosikia ulifanya Kapernaumu.'"
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Najua mtaniambia ule msemo wa zamani, 'Daktari, kwanza jiponye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!' Mtasema, 'Tumesikia mambo uliyofanya Kapernaumu. Fanya mambo hayo hayo hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani!'"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 틀림없이 이 속담을 나에게 말할 것이다. '의사야, 너 자신을 고쳐라. 우리가 가버나움에서 일어났다고 들은 일들을 여기 네 고향에서도 하여라.'"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 분명히 '의사야, 네 병이나 고쳐라' 하는 속담을 나에게 들이댈 것이다. 그리고 '네가 가버나움에서 했다고 우리가 들은 일들을 여기 네 고향에서도 해 보아라' 하고 말할 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 틀림없이 나에게 '의사야, 먼저 네 몸부터 고쳐라!' 하는 옛말을 할 것이다. 또 '네가 가버나움에서 한 일을 우리가 들었다. 그와 같은 일을 여기 네 고향에서도 해 보아라!' 하고 말할 것이다."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Chắc chắn các người sẽ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} câu tục ngữ này: 'Hỡi thầy thuốc, hãy chữa lấy chính mình! Những gì chúng tôi đã nghe là đã xảy ra tại Ca-bê-na-um, ông cũng hãy làm ở đây, tại quê hương của ông.'"
vi.B: Ngài nói với họ: "Hẳn các người sẽ đem câu tục ngữ này ra nói với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: 'Thầy thuốc ơi, hãy tự chữa cho mình đi!' Các người sẽ còn nói: 'Những việc chúng tôi nghe ông đã làm ở Ca-bê-na-um, ông hãy làm ở đây, tại quê nhà mình nữa đi.'"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ta biết chắc các người sẽ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} câu nói xưa nay: 'Bác sĩ ơi, trước hết hãy chữa bệnh cho chính mình đi!' Các người sẽ nói: 'Chúng tôi đã nghe về những việc ông làm ở Ca-bê-na-um. Ông hãy làm những việc đó ở đây, tại quê nhà của ông đi!'"

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Certamente vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dirão este provérbio: 'Médico, cura-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mesmo! O que ouvimos que aconteceu em Cafarnaum, faz também aqui na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} terra.'"
pt.B: Ele lhes disse: "Sem dúvida vocês vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} citar este ditado: 'Médico, cura-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mesmo!' E vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dizer: 'Faz aqui na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} própria cidade as coisas que ouvimos que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste em Cafarnaum.'"
pt.R: Jesus disse a eles: "Tenho certeza de que vocês vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dizer o velho ditado: 'Médico, cura primeiro a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mesmo!' Vocês vão dizer: 'Ouvimos falar do que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste em Cafarnaum. Faz as mesmas coisas aqui na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} própria cidade!'"

decisions.choice: Physician, heal yourself: prove what you claim by doing it for your own people
alternatives: a mocking call to cure his own illness
decisions.reason: A doctor who cannot heal himself is not trusted. Here the saying means: do your wonders here at home, among your own, and then we will believe.

decisions.choice: what we heard was done in Capernaum ...: still the words Jesus expects them to say
decisions.reason: The second part spells out what the proverb means for them, so it stands inside the quotation.

decisions.choice: what was done in Capernaum: works not yet told in Luke
decisions.reason: Luke tells the Capernaum events after this (4:31-41). The words assume Jesus had already worked there (4:14-15).

decisions.choice: Doctor
decisions.reason: "Doctor" is the everyday word; Literal keeps "Physician".

decisions.choice: And you will tell me (B); You will say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark that the second part is still what the people will say.

decisions.choice: Médecin at every level
decisions.reason: English Balanced and Readable say "Doctor" because "physician" is formal. French "médecin" is the everyday word, and the proverb is known in French in this form; "Docteur" is a way of addressing a doctor, not the name of the trade.

decisions.choice: mganga (L); daktari (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Mganga" is the older Swahili word for anyone who heals; Balanced and Readable use "daktari", as the English says "Doctor". The proverb means: prove your claims among your own people (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "câu tục ngữ" for the word elsewhere rendered "ngụ ngôn" (parable)
decisions.reason: The Greek word covers any comparison or saying; here it is a proverb (meaning decision), and "ngụ ngôn", kept for Jesus' parables (5:36), would mislead.

decisions.choice: "ông" for Jesus in the words Jesus expects his townspeople to say, with no setting span
decisions.reason: They challenge him to prove himself, so they would not call him Teacher; "ông" is polite but distant, as the style guide sets for those who do not believe, and words of address take no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: The words Jesus puts in the townspeople's mouths address him in 해라체 ("의사야", "하여라", "해 보아라")
alternatives: 합쇼체, as people normally speak to Jesus
decisions.reason: It is a proverb thrown at him as a challenge by people who see him as one of their own; the rule for people speaking to Jesus allows plain speech where the scene is hostile.

decisions.choice: "속담" (L, B), "옛말" (R) for parabolē here
decisions.reason: Here the word is a proverb, not a story; "비유" stays for Jesus's parables (5:36).

decisions.choice: Médico (every level)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "Doctor" as the everyday word. In Portuguese the everyday word is "médico"; "doutor" is a title of address and would not carry the proverb.

decisions.choice: tu ("cura-te", "faz", "tua")
decisions.reason: The townspeople's imagined words are addressed to Jesus, so they use "tu", as everyone who speaks to him does (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4).

source.text: εἶπεν δέ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He said then, Truly I say to you that no prophet acceptable is in the hometown of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
en.B: He added, "Truly I tell you, a prophet is never welcome in his own hometown.
en.R: Then Jesus said, "I tell you the truth, the people of a prophet's own town never welcome him.

es.L: Y dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ningún profeta es aceptado en su tierra.
es.B: Luego dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a ningún profeta lo reciben bien en su propio pueblo.
es.R: Después Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: la gente del pueblo de un profeta nunca lo recibe bien.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « En vérité, je vous le dis : aucun prophète n’est bien reçu dans sa patrie.
fr.B: Il ajouta : « En vérité, je vous le dis, un prophète n’est jamais bien accueilli dans sa propre ville.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a dit : « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : les gens de la ville d’un prophète ne l’accueillent jamais bien.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Kweli nawaambia kwamba hakuna nabii aliye na kibali katika mji wa kwao.
sw.B: Aliongeza, "Kweli nawaambia, nabii hakaribishwi kamwe katika mji wa kwao.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alisema, "Nawaambia ukweli, watu wa mji wa nabii mwenyewe hawamkaribishi kamwe.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 어떤 예언자도 자기 고향에서는 환영받지 못한다.
ko.B: 예수께서 또 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 예언자는 자기 고향에서 환영받지 못한다.
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 예언자는 자기가 자란 고향 사람들에게 결코 환영받지 못한다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, không một nhà tiên tri nào được chấp nhận tại quê hương mình.
vi.B: Ngài nói tiếp: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, không nhà tiên tri nào được đón tiếp tại quê nhà mình.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta nói thật với các người: người cùng quê với một nhà tiên tri không bao giờ đón tiếp người ấy.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Em verdade eu lhes digo que nenhum profeta é aceito na sua própria terra.
pt.B: E acrescentou: "Em verdade eu lhes digo: nenhum profeta é bem recebido na sua própria terra.
pt.R: Depois Jesus disse: "Eu garanto a vocês: o povo da cidade de um profeta nunca o recebe bem.

decisions.choice: Truly: a Hebrew word (amen) that confirms what follows
decisions.reason: Elsewhere "amen" agrees with what has just been said. Jesus uses it to introduce his own words with authority. This is the first time in Luke.

decisions.choice: acceptable: welcomed, received with favor
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "favor" in "the year of the Lord's favor" (4:19). The Lord's year of welcome is announced, but the prophet himself is not welcomed at home.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering, as in John.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's single "amen" (meaning decision m1), the same in every Gospel.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R) (for the whole book)
alternatives: Je vous le dis en vérité
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark. "Amen" at the start of a saying is not French usage; the set phrase keeps the solemn opening at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's single "amen" (meaning decision m1), the same in every Gospel.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R) for "Truly I tell you"
alternatives: Quả thật, Ta bảo các người
decisions.reason: The settled form for the single amen saying, as in Mark (9:1).

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R) for "Amen I say to you", through Luke
decisions.reason: The formula settled for Mark and John in Korean; Luke has the single amen.

decisions.choice: "예언자"
decisions.reason: The modern word, as in Mark and John (Korean style guide, Settled).

decisions.choice: Em verdade eu lhes digo (L, B); Eu garanto a vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The formula settled for the Gospels (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6), first used in Luke here. Readable's "Eu garanto a vocês" keeps the solemn assurance in plain words.

source.text: ἐπ’ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν, καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.

records.literal_gloss: In truth then I say to you, many widows were in the days of Elijah in the Israel, when was shut the heaven for years three and months six, as came a famine great upon all the land, \v 26 and to none of them was sent Elijah except to Zarephath of the Sidon to a woman widow.

en.L: But in truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land, \v 26 and Elijah was sent to none of them except to Zarephath of Sidon, to a woman [who was] a widow.
en.B: But I tell you in truth: in Elijah's day, when the sky stayed shut for three years and six months and a great famine struck the whole land, Israel had many widows. \v 26 Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to a widow at Zarephath in the land of Sidon.
en.R: Here is the truth. In the time of Elijah no rain fell for three and a half years, and there was very little food anywhere in the land. Israel had many widows then. \v 26 But God did not send Elijah to any of them. Instead, God sent him to a widow in the town of Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, outside Israel.

es.L: Pero de verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: había muchas viudas en los días de Elías en Israel, cuando el cielo quedó cerrado durante tres años y seis meses, al sobrevenir un hambre grande sobre toda la tierra, \v 26 y Elías no fue enviado a ninguna de ellas, excepto a Sarepta de Sidón, a una mujer [que era] viuda.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo con toda verdad: en tiempos de Elías, cuando el cielo permaneció cerrado tres años y seis meses y un hambre terrible azotó todo el país, había en Israel muchas viudas. \v 26 Sin embargo, Elías no fue enviado a ninguna de ellas, sino a una viuda de Sarepta, en la región de Sidón.
es.R: Esta es la verdad. En tiempos de Elías no llovió durante tres años y medio, y casi no había comida en ninguna parte del país. En ese tiempo había muchas viudas en Israel. \v 26 Pero Dios no envió a Elías a ninguna de ellas. En cambio, Dios lo envió a una viuda del pueblo de Sarepta, en la tierra de Sidón, fuera de Israel.

fr.L: Mais en vérité je vous le dis : il y avait beaucoup de veuves en Israël aux jours d’Élie, quand le ciel a été fermé pendant trois ans et six mois, quand une grande famine est survenue sur tout le pays, \v 26 et Élie n’a été envoyé vers aucune d’elles, sinon à Sarepta de Sidon, vers une femme veuve.
fr.B: Mais je vous le dis en vérité : au temps d’Élie, quand le ciel est resté fermé trois ans et six mois et qu’une grande famine a frappé tout le pays, il y avait beaucoup de veuves en Israël. \v 26 Pourtant, Élie n’a été envoyé chez aucune d’elles, mais chez une veuve de Sarepta, dans le pays de Sidon.
fr.R: Voici la vérité. À l’époque d’Élie, il n’a pas plu pendant trois ans et demi, et il n’y avait presque plus rien à manger dans tout le pays. Il y avait alors beaucoup de veuves en Israël. \v 26 Mais Dieu n’a envoyé Élie chez aucune d’elles. Il l’a envoyé chez une veuve de la ville de Sarepta, dans le pays de Sidon, en dehors d’Israël.

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwa kweli, kulikuwa na wajane wengi siku za Eliya katika Israeli, wakati anga lilipofungwa kwa miaka mitatu na miezi sita, njaa kuu ilipotokea juu ya nchi nzima, \v 26 na Eliya hakupelekwa kwa hata mmoja wao, ila Sarepta ya Sidoni, kwa mwanamke [aliyekuwa] mjane.
sw.B: Lakini nawaambia hakika: katika siku za Eliya, anga lilipokaa limefungwa kwa miaka mitatu na miezi sita, na njaa kali ikaikumba nchi yote, Israeli ilikuwa na wajane wengi. \v 26 Hata hivyo Eliya hakutumwa kwa yeyote kati yao, bali kwa mjane mmoja wa Sarepta katika nchi ya Sidoni.
sw.R: Huu ndio ukweli. Wakati wa Eliya mvua haikunyesha kwa miaka mitatu na nusu, na chakula kilikuwa haba sana kila mahali nchini. Wakati huo Israeli ilikuwa na wajane wengi. \v 26 Lakini Mungu hakumtuma Eliya kwa yeyote kati yao. Badala yake, Mungu alimtuma kwa mjane mmoja katika mji wa Sarepta, katika nchi ya Sidoni, nje ya Israeli.

ko.L: 그러나 참으로 내가 너희에게 말한다. 엘리야의 날들에, 하늘이 삼 년 육 개월 동안 닫혀서 온 땅에 큰 기근이 들었을 때, 이스라엘에는 과부가 많이 있었다. \v 26 그러나 엘리야는 그들 가운데 아무에게도 보내지지 않았고, 오직 시돈 지방 사렙다에 있는 한 과부인 여자에게 보내졌다.
ko.B: 내가 참으로 너희에게 말한다. 엘리야 시대에 하늘이 삼 년 육 개월 동안 닫혀서 온 땅에 큰 기근이 들었을 때, 이스라엘에는 과부가 많이 있었다. \v 26 그러나 엘리야는 그들 가운데 누구에게도 보내지지 않았고, 시돈 땅 사렙다에 사는 한 과부에게만 보내졌다.
ko.R: 내가 사실을 말해 주겠다. 엘리야 때에 삼 년 반 동안 비가 한 방울도 내리지 않았다. 그래서 온 땅에 먹을 것이 거의 없었다. 그때 이스라엘에는 과부가 많았다. \v 26 그러나 하나님께서는 엘리야를 그 과부들 가운데 누구에게도 보내지 않으셨다. 그 대신 엘리야를 시돈 땅 사렙다 마을에 사는 한 과부에게 보내셨다. 그곳은 이스라엘 밖이었다.

vi.L: Nhưng quả thật, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, có nhiều bà góa trong Y-sơ-ra-ên vào thời Ê-li, khi trời bị đóng lại ba năm sáu tháng, lúc nạn đói lớn xảy ra trên khắp xứ, \v 26 và Ê-li không được sai đến với một ai trong số họ, ngoại trừ đến Sa-rép-ta thuộc xứ Si-đôn, với một người đàn bà góa.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói cho các người biết sự thật: vào thời Ê-li, khi trời đóng lại suốt ba năm sáu tháng và nạn đói lớn xảy ra khắp xứ, trong Y-sơ-ra-ên có nhiều bà góa. \v 26 Thế nhưng Ê-li không được sai đến với một bà nào trong số họ, mà được sai đến với một bà góa ở Sa-rép-ta, thuộc xứ Si-đôn.
vi.R: Ta nói cho các người biết sự thật này. Vào thời Ê-li, trời không mưa suốt ba năm rưỡi, và khắp xứ gần như không còn gì để ăn. Lúc ấy, trong Y-sơ-ra-ên có rất nhiều bà góa. \v 26 Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời không sai Ê-li đến với bà nào trong số họ. Thay vào đó, Đức Chúa Trời sai ông đến với một bà góa ở thị trấn Sa-rép-ta, thuộc xứ Si-đôn, ở bên ngoài Y-sơ-ra-ên.

pt.L: Mas, em verdade, eu lhes digo: havia muitas viúvas em Israel nos dias de Elias, quando o céu foi fechado por três anos e seis meses, quando houve uma grande fome sobre toda a terra, \v 26 e Elias não foi enviado a nenhuma delas, a não ser a Sarepta de Sidom, a uma mulher viúva.
pt.B: Mas eu lhes digo a verdade: no tempo de Elias, quando o céu ficou fechado por três anos e seis meses e uma grande fome atingiu toda a terra, havia muitas viúvas em Israel. \v 26 Mas Elias não foi enviado a nenhuma delas, e sim a uma viúva de Sarepta, na região de Sidom.
pt.R: Esta é a verdade: no tempo de Elias não choveu durante três anos e meio, e quase não havia comida em toda a terra. Havia muitas viúvas em Israel naquela época. \v 26 Mas Deus não enviou Elias a nenhuma delas. Em vez disso, Deus o enviou a uma viúva da cidade de Sarepta, na região de Sidom, fora de Israel.

decisions.choice: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath: 1 Kings 17:8-24
decisions.reason: During the drought God sent Elijah to a widow in Zarephath, a town of Sidon, outside Israel. She fed him, and he raised her son. Jesus' point is that God sent his prophet to a foreigner rather than to Israel.

decisions.choice: three years and six months: the length of the drought in Jewish tradition
alternatives: the third year, as in 1 Kings 18:1
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 18:1 says the rain came "in the third year". James 5:17 also gives three years and six months; the times may be counted from different starting points.

decisions.choice: the sky was shut: no rain fell
alternatives: the heavens were closed to prayer
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as a store of rain that God closes (Deuteronomy 11:17; 1 Kings 8:35).

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, I am telling you something sure
decisions.reason: The phrase strengthens the statement, like "truly" in 4:24.

decisions.choice: God did not send ... God sent him
decisions.reason: Readable names who sent Elijah, which the passive implies.

decisions.choice: outside Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says why Zarephath matters, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the time first, then the widows, then the one widow
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set the scene first so that the contrast in 4:26 stands out.

decisions.choice: passé composé for the events Jesus retells ("a été fermé", "a frappé", "n’a été envoyé"), at every level
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: This is Jesus speaking, and the style guide keeps the tenses of speech for histories told inside a speech; the passé simple would turn his words into written narrative.

decisions.choice: anga
decisions.reason: Here the word means the sky that gave no rain (meaning decision m3); "mbingu" would suggest heaven as God's dwelling. Readable says plainly that no rain fell, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "quả thật" (L); "nói cho các người biết sự thật" (B, R) for "in truth"
decisions.reason: A different phrase from the amen of 4:24, so it does not take the settled amen wording.

decisions.choice: "Ê-li", "Sa-rép-ta", "Si-đôn"
decisions.reason: Protestant transliterations, in line with the style guide's names (Ê-li is in its list; Si-đôn as in Mark 3:8).

decisions.choice: "참으로 내가 너희에게 말한다" (L, B), "내가 사실을 말해 주겠다" (R) for "in truth I tell you"
alternatives: "진실로 너희에게 말한다", as for amen in 4:24
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different expression from the amen of 4:24, so Korean does not repeat the fixed amen formula.

decisions.choice: Protestant name forms "엘리야", "사렙다", "시돈"; "삼 년 육 개월" (L, B), "삼 년 반" (R)
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (Korean style guide, section 5).

decisions.choice: Sarepta, Sidom
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Portuguese forms (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 11 has "Sidom").

source.text: καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη, εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.

records.literal_gloss: And many lepers were in the Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.

en.L: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian."
en.B: And in the time of the prophet Elisha Israel had many people with leprosy, yet not one of them was made clean except Naaman, a man from Syria."
en.R: And in the time of the prophet Elisha many people in Israel had a skin disease. But none of them was healed. Only Naaman was healed, and he came from Syria."

es.L: Y había muchos leprosos en Israel en tiempos de Eliseo el profeta, y ninguno de ellos quedó limpio, excepto Naamán, el sirio».
es.B: Y en tiempos del profeta Eliseo había en Israel muchas personas con lepra, pero ninguna quedó limpia, salvo Naamán, un hombre de Siria».
es.R: Y en tiempos del profeta Eliseo, muchas personas en Israel tenían una enfermedad de la piel. Pero ninguna de ellas fue sanada. Solo Naamán fue sanado, y él era de Siria».

fr.L: Et il y avait beaucoup de lépreux en Israël au temps du prophète Élisée, et aucun d’eux n’a été purifié, sinon Naaman le Syrien. »
fr.B: Et au temps du prophète Élisée, il y avait en Israël beaucoup de gens atteints de la lèpre ; pourtant aucun d’eux n’a été purifié, sauf Naaman, un homme de Syrie. »
fr.R: Et à l’époque du prophète Élisée, beaucoup de gens en Israël avaient une maladie de peau. Mais aucun d’eux n’a été guéri. Seul Naaman a été guéri, et il venait de Syrie. »

sw.L: Na kulikuwa na wakoma wengi katika Israeli nyakati za Elisha nabii, na hakuna yeyote kati yao aliyetakaswa ila Naamani, yule Msiria."
sw.B: Na nyakati za nabii Elisha, Israeli ilikuwa na watu wengi wenye ukoma, lakini hakuna hata mmoja aliyetakaswa isipokuwa Naamani, mtu wa Siria."
sw.R: Tena wakati wa nabii Elisha, watu wengi katika Israeli walikuwa na ugonjwa wa ngozi. Lakini hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyeponywa. Naamani peke yake ndiye aliyeponywa, naye alikuwa mtu wa Siria."

ko.L: 그리고 엘리사 예언자 때에 이스라엘에는 나병 환자가 많이 있었으나, 시리아 사람 나아만 말고는 그들 가운데 아무도 깨끗하게 되지 않았다."
ko.B: 또 엘리사 예언자 시대에 이스라엘에는 악성 피부병에 걸린 사람이 많았다. 그러나 그들 가운데 깨끗해진 사람은 아무도 없었고, 시리아 사람 나아만만 깨끗해졌다."
ko.R: 또 엘리사 예언자 때에 이스라엘에는 나병, 곧 심한 피부병을 앓는 사람이 많았다. 그러나 그들 가운데 아무도 낫지 않았다. 오직 나아만만 병이 나았는데, 그는 시리아 사람이었다."

vi.L: Và có nhiều người phung trong Y-sơ-ra-ên vào thời nhà tiên tri Ê-li-sê, và không một ai trong số họ được sạch, ngoại trừ Na-a-man người Sy-ri."
vi.B: Vào thời nhà tiên tri Ê-li-sê, trong Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng có nhiều người mắc bệnh ngoài da nặng, nhưng không một ai trong số họ được sạch, ngoại trừ Na-a-man, một người từ Sy-ri."
vi.R: Vào thời nhà tiên tri Ê-li-sê, trong Y-sơ-ra-ên có nhiều người bị bệnh phong, một bệnh ngoài da rất nặng. Nhưng không ai trong số họ được chữa lành. Chỉ có Na-a-man được lành, mà ông lại là người Sy-ri."

pt.L: E havia muitos leprosos em Israel no tempo do profeta Eliseu, e nenhum deles foi purificado, a não ser Naamã, o sírio."
pt.B: E no tempo do profeta Eliseu havia em Israel muitas pessoas com lepra, mas nenhuma delas foi purificada, a não ser Naamã, um homem da Síria."
pt.R: E, no tempo do profeta Eliseu, muitas pessoas em Israel tinham uma doença de pele. Mas nenhuma delas foi curada. Só Naamã foi curado, e ele era da Síria."

decisions.choice: Elisha and Naaman: 2 Kings 5:1-14
decisions.reason: Naaman was the commander of the army of Aram, Israel's enemy. Elisha told him to wash in the Jordan, and he was healed. Again God's healing went to a foreigner.

decisions.choice: lepers: people with a serious skin disease
alternatives: only the disease now called leprosy (Hansen's disease)
decisions.reason: The word covered a range of skin diseases that made a person unclean under the Law (Leviticus 13).

decisions.choice: was cleansed: healed, and so clean under the Law
decisions.reason: Healing from the disease meant the person was no longer ritually unclean.

decisions.choice: had a skin disease ... was healed
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: lépreux, purifié (L, B); une maladie de peau, guéri (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark: cleansing means healing and being clean under the Law (m3), which "purifier" carries and "propre" would not. Readable uses plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "người phung" (L); "người mắc bệnh ngoài da nặng" (B); "bệnh phong, một bệnh ngoài da rất nặng" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:40: the Greek word covered several serious skin diseases (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Ê-li-sê", "Na-a-man", "Sy-ri"
decisions.reason: Protestant transliterations; "Sy-ri" as in Mark 7:26.

decisions.choice: "나병 환자" (L); "악성 피부병에 걸린 사람" (B); "나병, 곧 심한 피부병을 앓는 사람" (R), as in Mark 1:40
decisions.reason: The ancient disease was not only modern leprosy; the wording follows Mark in Korean, and "문둥병자" is now offensive.

decisions.choice: "시리아 사람 나아만"
decisions.reason: The modern name of the region is preferred where an older church form competes with it (Korean style guide, Settled); a reviewer may prefer "수리아".

source.text: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα, καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφ’ οὗ ἡ πόλις ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And were filled all with rage in the synagogue hearing these things, \v 29 and having risen up they drove out him outside the city, and led him to brow of the hill on which the town had been built of them, so as to throw down him;

en.L: And all in the synagogue were filled with rage on hearing these things, \v 29 and rising up they drove {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of the city and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to [the] brow of the hill on which their town had been built, so as to throw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down.
en.B: When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with fury. \v 29 They rose up and threw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of the town. They led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the edge of the hill where their town stood, meaning to hurl {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down from there.
en.R: When the people in the synagogue heard this, they were all very angry. \v 29 They got up and forced Jesus out of the town. Their town was built on a hill, and they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the edge of a cliff. They wanted to push {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} off.

es.L: Y todos en la sinagoga se llenaron de furor oyendo esto, \v 29 y poniéndose en pie {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} expulsaron fuera de la ciudad y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condujeron hasta [el] borde del cerro sobre el que estaba construida su ciudad, para arrojarlo abajo.
es.B: Al oír esto, todos los que estaban en la sinagoga se enfurecieron. \v 29 Se levantaron y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sacaron del pueblo a empujones. Lo llevaron hasta el borde del cerro donde estaba su pueblo, con la intención de arrojarlo desde allí.
es.R: Cuando la gente de la sinagoga oyó esto, todos se enojaron muchísimo. \v 29 Se levantaron y obligaron a Jesús a salir del pueblo. Su pueblo estaba construido sobre un cerro, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron hasta el borde de un precipicio. Querían empujarlo al vacío.

fr.L: Et tous furent remplis de fureur dans la synagogue en entendant ces choses, \v 29 et, s’étant levés, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chassèrent hors de la ville et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent jusqu’au bord escarpé de la colline sur laquelle leur ville était bâtie, pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} précipiter en bas.
fr.B: En entendant cela, tous ceux qui étaient dans la synagogue furent remplis de fureur. \v 29 Ils se levèrent et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} jetèrent hors de la ville. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent jusqu’au bord de la colline sur laquelle leur ville était bâtie, avec l’intention de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}y précipiter.
fr.R: Quand les gens de la synagogue ont entendu cela, ils se sont tous mis très en colère. \v 29 Ils se sont levés et ils ont poussé Jésus hors de la ville. Leur ville était construite sur une colline, et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont emmené au bord d’une falaise. Ils voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pousser dans le vide.

sw.L: Na wote walijawa na ghadhabu ndani ya sinagogi wakisikia mambo hayo, \v 29 na wakiisha kusimama, walimfukuza nje ya mji, wakamwongoza hadi ukingo wa mlima ambao juu yake mji wao ulikuwa umejengwa, ili wamtupe kutoka huko chini.
sw.B: Waliposikia hayo, wote waliokuwa katika sinagogi walikasirika mno. \v 29 Wakasimama, wakamfukuza nje ya mji. Wakampeleka mpaka ukingo wa mlima ambapo mji wao ulijengwa, wakikusudia kumtupa chini kutoka hapo.
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa katika sinagogi waliposikia hayo, wote walikasirika sana. \v 29 Walisimama, wakamlazimisha Yesu atoke nje ya mji. Mji wao ulikuwa umejengwa juu ya mlima, nao wakampeleka mpaka ukingo wa genge. Walitaka kumsukuma aanguke chini.

ko.L: 그러자 회당에 있던 모든 사람이 이 말을 듣고 분노로 가득 찼다. \v 29 그리고 일어나서 그분을 고을 밖으로 쫓아내고, 자기들의 고을이 세워져 있는 산의 벼랑 끝까지 그분을 끌고 가서, 그분을 밀어 떨어뜨리려고 하였다.
ko.B: 회당에 있던 사람들은 이 말을 듣고 모두 몹시 화가 났다. \v 29 그들은 일어나 예수를 동네 밖으로 내쫓았다. 그리고 그들의 동네가 자리 잡은 산의 벼랑 끝으로 예수를 끌고 가서, 밀어 떨어뜨리려고 하였다.
ko.R: 회당에 있던 사람들은 이 말을 듣고 모두 몹시 화가 났다. \v 29 그들은 일어나서 예수를 마을 밖으로 쫓아냈다. 그들의 마을은 산 위에 있었다. 그들은 예수를 낭떠러지 끝으로 끌고 갔다. 예수를 밀어 떨어뜨리려고 한 것이다.

vi.L: Và mọi người trong nhà hội, khi nghe những điều này, đều đầy cơn giận dữ, \v 29 và đứng dậy, họ đuổi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra khỏi thành và dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến mép ngọn đồi mà thành của họ được xây trên đó, để xô {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống.
vi.B: Nghe vậy, mọi người trong nhà hội đều giận dữ. \v 29 Họ đứng dậy, đuổi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra khỏi thị trấn, rồi dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến mép ngọn đồi nơi thị trấn của họ được xây lên, định xô {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống vực.
vi.R: Khi nghe những lời này, mọi người trong nhà hội đều rất tức giận. \v 29 Họ đứng dậy và đuổi Đức Giê-xu ra khỏi thị trấn. Thị trấn của họ được xây trên một ngọn đồi, và họ đưa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến bờ một vách đá. Họ muốn xô {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống.

pt.L: E todos na sinagoga ficaram cheios de fúria ao ouvir essas coisas \v 29 e, levantando-se, {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} expulsaram para fora da cidade e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram até [a] beira do monte sobre o qual a cidade deles tinha sido construída, para {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} atirarem dali para baixo.
pt.B: Ao ouvirem isso, todos na sinagoga ficaram furiosos. \v 29 Eles se levantaram e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} expulsaram da cidade. Depois {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram até a beira do monte onde a cidade deles ficava, com a intenção de {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} jogar lá de cima.
pt.R: Quando as pessoas na sinagoga ouviram isso, ficaram todas com muita raiva. \v 29 Elas se levantaram e obrigaram Jesus a sair da cidade. A cidade delas ficava num monte, e elas {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levaram até a beira de um penhasco. Queriam empurrá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} lá de cima.

decisions.choice: filled with rage: they see that God's favor reaches outsiders, and that Jesus will not do signs for them on demand
alternatives: anger at a personal insult only
decisions.reason: The stories of Elijah and Elisha say that God's prophets were sent beyond Israel. The praise of 4:22 turns to fury. This looks ahead to the gospel going to the nations in Acts.

decisions.choice: the brow of the hill on which their town was built: a slope or cliff near Nazareth
alternatives: a hill far from the town
decisions.reason: Nazareth lies on a hillside with steep slopes around it.

decisions.choice: to throw him down: perhaps the first step of a stoning
decisions.reason: A person to be stoned was sometimes first thrown down from a height. Luke says they meant to kill him.

decisions.choice: the edge of a cliff
decisions.reason: Readable says what the brow of the hill was, so that the danger is clear.

decisions.choice: "thành" (L); "thị trấn" (B, R) for the town
decisions.reason: Luke's word is used of any walled or unwalled town; Nazareth was small, and "thành" today suggests a city. Literal keeps the traditional word, as Mark does.

decisions.choice: "고을" (L), "동네" (B), "마을" (R) for polis, a small town, through Luke 4-5
decisions.reason: Nazareth and Capernaum were small towns; the three words follow Mark 1:33 in Korean.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.

records.literal_gloss: He but having passed through midst of them went on.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, atravesando por en medio de ellos, siguió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} camino.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi qua giữa họ mà ra đi.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} desceu a Cafarnaum, cidade da Galileia.

decisions.choice: went down to Capernaum: from the hill country to the lake shore

source.text: καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν·

records.literal_gloss: And he was teaching them on the Sabbaths;

en.B: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would teach the people on the Sabbath.

es.L: Y estaba enseñándoles en los sábados.

es.R: Allí enseñaba a la gente en el día de descanso, el sábado.

fr.B: Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait les gens le jour du sabbat.
fr.R: Là-bas, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait les gens le jour de repos, le sabbat.

sw.L: Na alikuwa akiwafundisha siku za Sabato.

decisions.choice: was teaching them on the Sabbaths: he taught on Sabbath days there
alternatives: he taught on one Sabbath only

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whom he taught.

decisions.choice: "안식일들에" (L), "안식일마다" (B)
decisions.reason: Here the plural means several Sabbaths in turn, as the meaning decision says, so Literal keeps it, unlike the idiom of 4:16.

en.R: The people were amazed at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke like someone with the right to command.

ko.L: 그리고 사람들은 그분의 가르침에 놀라고 있었다. 그분의 말씀이 권위가 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사람들은 그분의 가르침에 깜짝 놀랐다. 그분의 말씀에 권위가 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사람들은 예수께서 가르치시는 것을 듣고 놀랐다. 예수께서는 참된 권위를 가진 분처럼 말씀하셨기 때문이다.

vi.L: và họ kinh ngạc về sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì lời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thẩm quyền.
vi.B: Sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khiến họ sửng sốt, vì lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói có thẩm quyền.
vi.R: Dân chúng rất ngạc nhiên về điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói như một người có quyền ra lệnh.

pt.L: e eles ficavam admirados com o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} ensino, porque a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} palavra era com autoridade.
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} ensino os deixava admirados, pois havia autoridade no que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} dizia.
pt.R: As pessoas ficavam admiradas com o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ensinava, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} falava como alguém que tem o direito de dar ordens.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and power to speak for God
decisions.reason: His word has power to act, as the next scene shows: he commands spirits with authority (4:36). Mark 1:22 contrasts this with the teaching of the scribes.

decisions.choice: word: what he said, his message
decisions.reason: The noun means speech or message as a whole.

decisions.choice: like someone with the right to command
decisions.reason: Readable explains "authority".

decisions.choice: "권위" at every level for the authority of Jesus's word (4:32, 4:36)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22 and 1:27 in Korean, the same word marks the authority of his teaching and of his command over spirits.

pt.B: Na sinagoga havia um homem que tinha o espírito de um demônio impuro, e ele gritou com voz forte:
pt.R: Na sinagoga havia um homem com um demônio dentro dele. O demônio era um espírito mau. O homem deu um grito bem alto:

decisions.choice: a spirit of an unclean demon: a demon, an evil spirit that made him unclean
decisions.reason: Luke joins two ways of speaking: "unclean spirit" (4:36) and "demon" (4:35). "Unclean" means opposed to God's holiness, the opposite of the Holy One of God (4:34).

decisions.choice: he cried out: the demon speaks through the man
decisions.reason: The words that follow are the demon's ("us", "I know you").

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable's usual way of putting "unclean" here, since young readers would take "unclean" to mean dirty.

decisions.choice: demonio impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: "impuro" says that the demon made the man unclean (meaning decision m1) in today's Spanish, where "inmundo" sounds like filth; Readable says "maligno", as the English Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: un démon impur, un esprit impur (L, B); un esprit mauvais (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark. "Immonde" is old church language; Readable says "mauvais", as the English Readable says "evil", since "impur" suggests dirt to young readers.

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: "mchafu" says that the demon made the man unclean (meaning decision m1); Readable says "mbaya", as the English Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: "linh của một quỷ ô uế" (L); "linh quỷ ô uế" (B); "quỷ ... tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: Luke joins "spirit" and "unclean demon"; Literal and Balanced keep both words, with the settled "ô uế" for unclean, and Readable says "quỷ" and "tà linh", as Mark's Readable does for demons and unclean spirits.

decisions.choice: "더러운 귀신의 영" (L, B); "귀신" ... "악한 영" (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's phrase joins spirit, demon and unclean; Korean uses Mark's words for each: "귀신" for demon, "더러운 영" (L, B) and "악한 영" (R) for the unclean spirit (4:36).

decisions.choice: um espírito mau
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:23, Readable says "mau" where young readers would take "impuro" or "sujo" as dirt, following the English Readable "evil"; Literal and Balanced keep "impuro" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6).

source.text: Ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ;

records.literal_gloss: Ha, what to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene?

en.L: "Ha! What [is there] between us and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.B: "Ah! What have we to do with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.R: "Leave us alone, Jesus from Nazareth! Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering us?

es.L: «¡Ea! ¿Qué [hay] entre nosotros y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Jesús de Nazaret?
es.B: «¡Ah! ¿Qué tienes que ver con nosotros, Jesús de Nazaret?
es.R: «¡Déjanos en paz, Jesús de Nazaret! ¿Por qué nos molestas?

fr.L: « Ha ! Qu’[y a-t-il] entre nous et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Jésus de Nazareth ?
fr.B: « Ah ! Que nous veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, Jésus de Nazareth ?
fr.R: « Laisse-nous tranquilles, Jésus de Nazareth ! Pourquoi viens-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous déranger ?

sw.L: "Aha! Kuna nini kati yetu na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Yesu Mnazareti?
sw.B: "Lo! Una nini nasi, Yesu wa Nazareti?
sw.R: "Tuache, Yesu wa Nazareti! Kwa nini unatusumbua?

ko.L: "아! 우리와 당신 사이에 무슨 [상관이 있습니까], 나사렛 사람 예수여?

ko.R: "나사렛 예수여, 우리를 내버려 두십시오! 왜 우리를 괴롭힙니까?

vi.L: "Ôi! Giữa chúng tôi với ông có [liên quan] gì, Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét?
vi.B: "Ôi! Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, ông với chúng tôi có liên quan gì?
vi.R: "Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, hãy để chúng tôi yên! Sao ông lại quấy rầy chúng tôi?

pt.L: "Ah! Que [há] entre nós e {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Jesus de Nazaré?
pt.B: "Ah! O que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} queres conosco, Jesus de Nazaré?
pt.R: "Deixa-nos em paz, Jesus de Nazaré! Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vens nos incomodar?

decisions.choice: Ha: a cry of alarm or anger
alternatives: Let us alone! (from a verb meaning to let go)
decisions.reason: The word is a cry. It may also be read as a command, "Leave us alone!", which Readable follows.

decisions.choice: What is there between us and you?: what do you have to do with us; leave us alone
alternatives: what do we have in common?
decisions.reason: The phrase is found in the Old Testament when someone rejects another's interference (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: us: the demon speaks for the demons as a group
decisions.reason: Jesus' coming threatens all of them.

decisions.choice: Leave us alone! ... Why are you bothering us?
alternatives: Ha! What is there between us and you?
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cry and the idiom mean.

decisions.choice: the demon says "Giê-xu" without "Đức", "ông" for "you" and "chúng tôi" for itself (4:34)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 1:24, which has the same Greek: a hostile speaker does not honour Jesus, and words of address take no deity_pronoun span. The wording follows Mark's.

decisions.choice: "Ôi!" for the cry
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says alarm or anger; "Ôi!" carries alarm, which suits the question that follows.

decisions.choice: The demon speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "당신", and no honorific -시- or "께" in its statements about him, as in Mark 1:24
alternatives: 해라체, as the devil speaks in 4:3-12
decisions.reason: The demon is afraid and acknowledges who Jesus is; the choice settled for Mark keeps the synoptic parallel alike.

decisions.choice: tu, ti
decisions.reason: The demon, like everyone who speaks to Jesus, uses "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), as in Mark 1:24; the hostility is in the words. Readable's "Deixa-nos em paz" is the "tu" imperative.

source.text: ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς;
